Code 57/3/3, BIOLOGY (Theory), 3 hours, 70 marks, 31 printed pages, 33 questions); idx 1 is the Hindi instructions; every ODD index 1-29 is the Hindi facing page. The contact sheet, a word scan of the text layer of every odd page (Krutidev-encoded Hindi only: zero hits for 'the', 'which', 'following', 'of', 'and' on all fifteen) and full-size reads of every even page show no English overflow onto an odd page, no parity inversion, and an English final page (idx 30, Q33(b)). Born-digital paper: the text layer was a DRAFT only (it drops quoted labels, curly-quoted phrases, en dashes, superscripts and whole stem lines in Q8, Q20(a), Q25, Q29(iii)-(iv), Q30(i), Q30(iv), Q32(a)(ii)-(iii)); every row was read on the full-size page. Instruction (viii) prints the count: 1 internal choice in Section B, 1 in C, 2 in D, 3 in E = seven alternatives (Q20, Q26, Q29(iv), Q30(iv), Q31, Q32, Q33), each confirmed against a bare OR in the marking scheme and on the page. All Section-D sub-parts print 1 mark each. Primary marks: A16 + B10 + C21 + D8 + E15 = 70. Section-A key read on the scheme IMAGE (ms idx 2) and from the scheme's text layer, agreeing on all 16 entries: C A [A//B] D C A B [none] [B//D] B A A A B D A. Q3 is a dual key (a) // (b), shipped B; Q8 prints no letter ('Marks to be awarded if attempted .'), shipped with _noCorrectOption; Q9 is the dual key (b) // (d), shipped D as the opener did. FOLLOWER of 57/3/1: 32 of the 46 rows are 57/3/1 questions, each confirmed on this paper's own page and given 57/3/1's stem, context and options byte for byte (this paper's Q1 = 57/3/1 Q4, Q6 = Q12, Q7 = Q11, Q8 = Q10, Q9 = Q7, Q11 = Q8, Q12 = Q3, Q17 = Q17, Q19 = Q19, Q20a/b = Q21a/b, Q22 = Q28, Q23 = Q27, Q24 = Q26, Q25 = Q25, Q26a/b = Q22a/b (this page prints 'in a eukaryote cell', as 57/3/1 does), Q27 = Q23, Q29i-ivb = Q29i-ivb, Q30i-ivb = Q30i-ivb, Q31a/b = Q32a/b, Q32a/b = Q31a/b); the MCQ matches carry the same options in the same order and this scheme keys the same letter (or, for Q8, the same keyless void). The assertion-reason context and options are 57/3/1's (same printed wording; this page prints the code letters in lower case and italicises 'not'). NEW on this set: Q2 (black pepper perisperm), Q3 (most and least fertile days, figure), Q4 (Mesozoic plants), Q5 (Hershey and Chase label), Q10 (not a hotspot), Q13-Q16 (four new assertion-reason pairs), Q18 (biogas), Q21 (Amazon fires), Q28 (journey of the zygote), Q33a (embryo sac; outbreeding devices) and Q33b (Sertoli and Leydig cells; hormonal control of spermatogenesis). Observe the following line diagram depicting the 28 days menstrual cycle of a healthy young woman.
Select the option of days on which this woman would be most and least fertile.

options.label: A
options.text: Most fertile days: 14 – 21; Least fertile days: 1 – 7

options.label: B
options.text: Most fertile days: 10 – 17; Least fertile days: 21 – 28

options.label: C
options.text: Most fertile days: 1 – 7; Least fertile days: 14 – 21

options.label: D
options.text: Most fertile days: 21 – 28; Least fertile days: 7 – 14

questions._cbseVoided: (a) / Most fertile days 14-21, least fertile days 1-7 // (b) / Most fertile days 10-17, least fertile days 21-28
questions._figure: REQUIRED:a horizontal arrowed day axis ticked at 1, 7, 14, 21 and 28 (days), with a vertical line rising at day 1 captioned 'Menstruation' and another at day 14 captioned 'Ovulation'. The drawing gives the premise (where ovulation falls), not the answer, so it is described in full. Page idx 4.
questions._flag: DUAL KEY: the scheme accepts (a) or (b) with no note. The options print as a two-column table headed 'Most fertile days' and 'Least fertile days'; each option is written here with both headings. Shipped B, not the first printed, because it is the letter that teaches the syllabus point: NCERT gives days 10 to 17 of the cycle, around ovulation, as the period when the chances of fertilisation are very high (the basis of periodic abstinence). Days 14 to 21 run mostly after the ovum has ceased to be viable, which is why (a) is the weaker reading; the solution explains why it was also credited.

questions.stem: Which one of the following was not present during the Mesozoic Era of the geological time scale ?
questions._flag: The scheme keys (d) Bryophytes. Bryophytes arose in the Palaeozoic and survive today, so they were in fact present during the Mesozoic, as were ferns, horsetails and ginkgos; the key treats the bryophytes, the oldest and simplest group in the list, as the odd one out. Kept as the scheme keys it; the solution says so.

questions._flag: The scheme keys (a). Both statements are true; the Reason gives the route by which the bacterium spreads (food and water), and Mary Mallon, a cook, spread it through the food she prepared. What NCERT stresses about her, that she was a healthy CARRIER, is not in the Reason, so (b) is a defensible reading. Kept as the scheme keys it; the solution says so.

questions._flag: EITHER OF TWO ANSWERS ACCEPTED for part (a): besides the explanation, this scheme credits the statement that GIFT has no role in a test tube baby programme (unlike 57/3/1, it prints no such alternative for IUI). questions._figure: REQUIRED:a three-generation pedigree of circles (females) and squares (males) with every individual lettered: Generation I 'B' and 'A' as a couple; Generation II their children 'C', 'D' and 'E', with 'E' married to 'F'; Generation III the children of 'E' and 'F', namely 'G', 'H' and 'I'. questions._flag: The scheme keys this as SEX-LINKED, reasoning that more males are affected. The chart (affected males only, passed from an affected father to a son in two generations) is equally consistent with an autosomal recessive reading, and under the sex-linked reading both unaffected mothers 'B' and 'F' must be carriers. The solution follows the scheme and closes with that note.
